claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was bishop of Alexandria from 412 until his death in 444.
Cyril was born around 375–80 in Alexandria.
Cyril succeeded his uncle Theophilus as bishop of Alexandria in 412.
Cyril's commentary on the Psalms is no longer extant in its full form, but survives as numerous fragments from the catenae.
The fragments of Cyril's Commentary on the Psalms are preserved in the Palestinian and monophysite catenae.
In the late eleventh century, Nicetas of Heraclea drew material from Cyril's commentary for his own chain on the Psalms.

The only independent text of the fragments is found in Laudianus gr. 42, an anthology manuscript in Oxford dating from the late eleventh to early twelfth century, where the Cyrillian portion appears on folios 290-302.
In the Proemium of his Commentary on the Psalms, Cyril writes that the text of the Psalms is overflowing with narratives concerning Christ the Saviour.
The patristic understanding of the Incarnation owes more to Cyril of Alexandria than to any other individual theologian.
Cyril was named a doctor of the church in 1882.
